strategyReview: Working: the live WEEKEND_HL_FUNDING_REVERSION_LONG book remains the strongest engine family (401/576 clean wins, avg 0.15%; shadows 188/253, avg 0.99%), ONE_TOUCH_HIGH_EDGE_NO is profitable when measured on contract premium (4/4 live; 110/179 gated shadows), and the outcome-panel NO edges are robust in near-dated mid-price cuts. Failing: raw single-threshold weekend funding shadow variants (CBRS/MU/AAPL), HYPE-confirmed BTC continuation longs, Polymarket proxy short shadows, and one-touch variants graded as spot-decline calls are all at or below base. The common causes are entering before funding actually turns, treating contract-premium edges as spot-directional signals, and trusting HYPE risk-on confirmation too late.

failureClusters.evidence: CBRS H-539 is 14/31 (45%), MU H-535 is 7/19 (37%), AAPL H-537 is 13/25 (52%). The loss examples repeatedly start from only mildly negative or even positive funding and fail to normalize into a >2% spot move.
failureClusters.recommendation: Do not promote these as standalone < -10 variants. Refine to relative funding distress or confirmed direction change, or fold them back into the broader weekend funding family.

failureClusters.theme: HYPE risk-on confirmed BTC continuation longs
failureClusters.evidence: cross_asset_iv_compression_vol_expansion is 9/25 (36%). Examples show BTC near highs with HYPE above its SMA, then BTC either declines or stays below the 2% continuation hurdle.
failureClusters.recommendation: Treat near-high HYPE risk-on participation as late-stage/exhaustion evidence, not continuation confirmation. Test contrarian or kill this family.

failureClusters.evidence: PC_RATIO_EXTREME_LOW_PM_PROXY_SHORT 1/18 avg -6.19%; FUNDING_EXTREME_LONG_PM_PROXY_SHORT 3/23 avg -2.94%; OPT_IV_GT_PM_IV_DOWNSIDE 2/16 avg -9.95%; RELATIVE_VALUE_HEATMAP 4/15 avg -8.09%; ONE_TOUCH_HIGH_EDGE_YES 2/9 avg -25.90%.
failureClusters.recommendation: Stop promoting these proxy-short shadows. They cluster losses and mostly represent mis-specified spot-decline bets rather than tradeable PM premium decay.

failureClusters.theme: Contract-edge signals graded as spot moves
failureClusters.evidence: H-534 has 8/23 scorable wins and 7 unscorable tests; examples show positive contract premium behavior while the spot-decline criterion fails.
failureClusters.recommendation: Re-author one-touch NO and other contract-edge hypotheses with contract P&L predictions, not 'spot will decline >2%' predictions.

hypothesisReviews.observation: H-539 fired on CBRS funding readings that were only mildly negative or already positive and then often worsened; the spot-decline/higher funding criterion won only 14/31.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: A standalone CBRS funding reading below -10% reliably normalizes within two days and forces >2% CBRS spot gain.

hypothesisReviews.observation: AAPL tests show poor timing: many entries started around 5.5% funding and failed to normalize; 13/25 wins is not enough for promotion.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: AAPL funding below -10% on any day reliably normalizes and forces a >2% AAPL spot gain within 2 days.

hypothesisReviews.observation: MU is the weakest of the weekend funding shadow singles at 7/19; most triggers were not in a truly extreme funding state and the >2% spot claim did not materialize.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: A single MU funding reading below -10% reliably normalizes and produces >2% MU spot gain within 2 days.

hypothesisReviews.observation: H-534 burns unscorable tests and its scorable losses show the issue is instrument choice: the contract edge can be profitable as premium decay, but the test demands a >2% GOLD spot decline.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: A large underlying-cap edge on upside one-touch NO contracts pays via a >2% GOLD spot decline within 2 days, rather than via contract premium decay.

hypothesisReviews.observation: The HYPE-confirmed BTC long family is 9/25. Near 7d highs with HYPE above its SMA, BTC frequently failed to make >2% and sometimes reversed.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: HYPE spot above its 24h SMA with stable OI is an independent confirmation of durable BTC upside rather than late-stage FOMO or overextension.

hypothesisReviews.observation: The PM IV compression family is 4/15. Slots with BTC PM IV z-score below -1.5 frequently produced sub-2% absolute moves or no snapback.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: BTC PM IV below its 30-day mean by more than 1.5 standard deviations reliably leads to a >2% absolute spot move within 3 days.

journalEntry: Tonight's main lesson is instrument and timing discipline. The live weekend funding book still works, but single-asset shadow refinements are failing because they use raw < -10 readings instead of relative funding distress. One-touch NO edges must be tested as contract premium fade, not spot decline. HYPE risk-on confirmation is not a valid BTC continuation filter. The outcome-panel NO edge remains the highest-priority promotion path; I added clean panel siblings for the near-dated, mid-price, tight-spread, and sub-point-edge cuts rather than inventing off-theme ideas. No parameter changes: weekend-clustered evidence is still too thin to move weekendFundingEntryPct, and risk changes are not justified yet.
